content.rendered:
Every morning at 6AM (UTC+8), Gospelbuzz publishes a daily devotional to help you start your day grounded in Scripture. Here is a look back at this week’s seven devotionals — one theme, one scripture, one prayer for each day. Catch up on any you missed, or share one with someone who needs it today.

☀️ Sunday, April 19 — Come to Me

Scripture: Matthew 11:28
“Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.”

Jesus did not say “sort yourself out and then come.” He said come — as you are, weary and burdened. The rest is His to give. You do not manufacture it. You receive it.

📖 Read the full devotional →

☀️ Monday, April 20 — New Every Morning

Scripture: Lamentations 3:22–23
“His mercies are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.”

Jeremiah wrote these words in the middle of Jerusalem’s destruction — surrounded by rubble, grief and loss. And yet. Mercies new every morning. Not because circumstances improved, but because God is faithful regardless of circumstances. Whatever yesterday held, this morning is new.

📖 Read the full devotional →

☀️ Tuesday, April 21 — Lean Not on Your Own Understanding

Scripture: Proverbs 3:5–6
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight.”

Your understanding is real — and limited. His understanding is infinite. Leaning on your own understanding is not strength. It is the subtle pride of preferring your own map when the Maker of the territory is offering to guide you. Trust with all your heart. Not most of it.

📖 Read the full devotional →

☀️ Wednesday, April 22 — Wings Like Eagles

Scripture: Isaiah 40:31
“But those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint.”

The promise is not that you will never feel tired. It is that those who wait on the Lord — who hope, who trust, who remain in His presence — will be renewed. Not just survive. Soar. The eagle does not flap harder into the wind. It spreads its wings and lets the current carry it. That is the picture of faith.

📖 Read the full devotional →

☀️ Thursday, April 23 — Fearfully and Wonderfully Made

Scripture: Psalm 139:14
“I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made; your works are wonderful, I know that full well.”

David wrote this as a declaration, not a question. He did not say “I wonder if I am wonderfully made.” He said I know it — full well. In a world that will tell you every day that you are not enough, not beautiful enough, not capable enough — the Word says you are God’s handiwork, crafted with awe and intention. Believe it.

📖 Read the full devotional →

☀️ Friday, April 24 — God’s Handiwork

Scripture: Ephesians 2:10
“For we are God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.”

The Greek word for handiwork is poiema — from which we get the word “poem.” You are not an accident. You are not a rough draft. You are a poem — crafted with intention, with meaning in every line. And the works God prepared for you to walk in are not burdens. They are the reason you were made.

📖 Read the full devotional →

☀️ Saturday, April 25 — He Is Singing Over You

Scripture: Zephaniah 3:17
“The Lord your God is with you, the Mighty Warrior who saves. He will take great delight in you; in his love he will no longer rebuke you, but will rejoice over you with singing.”

Let that settle. The God who created the universe — the Mighty Warrior who saves — takes great delight in you. He rejoices over you. With singing. This is not a God who barely tolerates you. This is a Father who sings over His child. On the days you feel most undeserving, He is singing the loudest. 🙏
